question: A call goes up to a satellite 35,786 km high and back down. At 300,000 km/s, how many milliseconds does that hop take?
answer: About 239 milliseconds, before the other person has even heard a word.
move: Some delays are set by distance, and no upgrade can remove them.
ask: Which delay in my life am I trying to fix with effort, when it is built into the setup?
trap: Radio is light-fast, so any delay must be the equipment's fault.
hint: Count the distance both ways, then divide by the speed.
steps: About 239 milliseconds, before the other person has even heard a word.
reference: Pratt, Bostian & Allnutt, Satellite Communications, 2nd edition, Wiley, 2003
